rationale: shared.give introduces place routes and ownership modes, and given.programs supplies Delta and ordered-program/class-table notation. This unit gives domains for C, f, x, n and grammar for p, e, and t before using them. The selected Place has variable and field forms; Value has give, giveShare, and recursive new; Statement holds exactly one destination and Value; Program pairs a class table with a statement list. No primitive values, assignment, calls, scopes, or borrowing forms occur. Class.fields is an ordered list without field types. The supporting Eval and EvalArgs definitions in context:lean/Shared/Step.lean confirm that giveShare performs Give then changes the result to shared, and that constructor arguments evaluate left to right, including nested constructors. Step.letValue requires a fresh destination after evaluation, matching runtime freshness rather than promising static acceptance of every statement list. The prose correctly requires a variable before give-sharing a newly constructed object because giveShare accepts a Place, not an arbitrary Value.
